tools.label: Typographic arrows:
n.dropwrong1: And what exactly is that supposed to do?
n.typo_done: Yes, yes, you already found that one. Stop rubbing it in.
h.none: No ideas right now. Odd: I usually have too many.
card.ch11.label: Chapter 11
card.ch11.title: The Type Case
end.ch11.title: End of Chapter 11
end.ch11.body:
The Pencil is safe in the margin and has finally said what she wants: to write the last page.
In Chapter 12 the Proofreader turns on the Narrator.
ana.label: LICNEP
page.p33.title: Type case lid
page.p33.intro: The lid opens when the password is set in movable type. Tap one letter, then another, to swap them.
page.p33.margin: the proofreader always uses the same word. the one he hates most
page.p34.title: Type case index
page.p34.intro: Every character has its drawer, and every drawer its label.
page.p34.list:
A ......... drawer 1
B ......... drawer 2
...
LICNEP .... drawer 31 (sealed)
page.p34.locked: Drawer 31's label is under the glass lid.
page.p35.title: Margin
page.p35.intro: White space at the reader's disposal. By contract, the Proofreader does not correct margins.
page.p35.pencil: here i am. nobody can touch me here.
art.tc.title: TYPE CASSE
n.i1: We got into the print shop through the back. This is the movable type case.
n.i2: Yes, forward. But quietly. The Proofreader has gone for a coffee. No sugar, I imagine.
p.i1: i'm here! in a drawer! in the dark!
n.i3: The Pencil! The Proofreader filed her like any old character. But there's a glass lid, with a letter lock.
n.i4: Page 33: the combination is set in movable type. All the letters are there. In a muddle.
n.empty1: The print shop floor. Full of fallen commas.
n.empty2: Nothing there. The letters are all in the drawers.
n.page_wrong: Not on this page. The Pencil goes in the margin, page 35: the Proofreader can't correct there.
n.tool1: The arrows won't help here. Letters are moved by hand.
n.typo_case: "Casse". An extra S, filed in the wrong drawer.
n.typo_type: "Tpye". So movable the letters moved themselves.
n.lock: The lid's letter lock. The combination is on page 33.
n.lock_open: The lid is open. It smells of lead and ink.
n.cabinet: Hundreds of drawers, each with its letter. The Proofreader loves alphabetical order.
n.cabinet_open: All the drawers in order. Except one.
n.glass: The glass lid is in the way. The combination first.
p.knock: knock knock. i'm in the one with the wrong label.
p.drawer: get me out of here. put me in the margin, he can't touch me there.
n.drawer_empty: Drawer 31 is empty. The Proofreader is in for a nasty surprise.
n.lock1: "OPEN". The lid lifts. The word the Proofreader hates most.
p.lock: my drawer is number 31. he got the label wrong on purpose, so nobody would find me.
n.lock2: Page 34: the label says "LICNEP". The letters need putting back in order.
p.label: finally, a bit of light.
n.label2: There she is. Smaller than I thought. And angrier.
p.x1: thank you. the margin is the safest place in the book.
n.x1: Now tell us the truth. What's favour number three?
p.x2: i want to write the last page. the one the proofreader wants to leave blank.
n.x2: The Narrator writes the last page! It's a tradition! ...I think.
p.x3: then let's write it together. but first get your voice back. you're about to lose it.
c.x1: Drawer 31 is empty. Very well. Then I shall start with the Narrator.
h.lock.1: The glass lid has a letter lock. The combination is on page 33.
h.lock.2: The letters are the right ones, but muddled. It's the word the Proofreader hates most.
h.lock.3: Tap the letters in pairs to swap them until they spell "OPEN".
h.label.1: The Pencil's drawer has the wrong label. The index is on page 34.
h.label.3: Swap the label's letters until they spell "PENCIL".
h.rescue.1: The Pencil is free, but the Proofreader will be back soon.
h.rescue.2: There's a part of the book that, by contract, the Proofreader doesn't correct.
h.rescue.3: Drag the Pencil from the drawer onto page 35 of the manual: the Margin.
